headline: Canadian legislator reads LLM prompt instruction aloud in floor speech
summary: A New Brunswick MLA accidentally read an AI prompt instruction into the legislative record, sparking debate about the growing divide in elite vs. public AI use.
details: Bill Oliver, a Progressive Conservative member of the legislative assembly of New Brunswick, inadvertently read an AI prompt instruction aloud during a speech. The phrase, "here’s a more natural, flowing version of that section that reads like a legislative speech rather than a series of short points," is typical of LLM style suggestions.

The incident went largely unnoticed at the time but gained traction on social media, with Canadian news outlets now highlighting it. The Toronto Star described the event as indicative of a societal divide between elites who delegate duties to AI and the public who find it objectionable.

This marks a notable instance of AI use being revealed in an embarrassing public manner, joining a trend seen with lawyers, authors, journalists, and academics whose reliance on LLMs has led to errors or scrutiny.

A Duke University study found that workers often hide their AI use due to perceptions of laziness or replaceability, suggesting a societal unease with the increasing integration of AI in professional tasks.
